newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ANGOLA, Dec 2 - Luanda - No berthing delays for any type of vessel. Lobito, Namibe - Ports quiet with no berthing delays. Cabinda - Jetty clear for operations. Crude oil terminal loading according to plan. Soyo - Kwanda base working normally. Supplies arriving via Luanda and Pt. Noire. No direct service from Northern Europe or South Africa operating. Lombo este terminal loading according to schedule. Palanca crude terminal loading according to schedule.

ISRAEL, Dec 3 - No labour problems. Haifa - Sixteen vessels operating at berth of which 7 general cargo (1 loading, 6 discharging), 2 bulkers discharging, 5 containers, 2 tankers. 3 Vessels waiting at anchorage of which 2 to discharge (1 general cargo, 1 bulker), 1 containers. 2 Vessels bunkering, 1 under repair/dry-docked, 4 awaiting orders. 2 Vessels due with 2-4 days delay expected. Ashdod - Seventeen vessels operating at berth of which 9 general cargo (all discharging). 3 Bulkers (2 loading, 1 discharging), 2 containers, 1 car carrier, 2 tankers. 8 Vessels waiting at anchorage of which 2 general cargo, 2 bulkers, 4 containers, 2-4 days berthing delay expected. Eilat - Two vessels operating at berth of which 1 tanker, 1 passenger vessel.
JORDAN, Dec 1 - Aqaba - Four vessels loading at berth, 7 discharging at berth, 2 waiting at anchorage to discharge.

MOZAMBIQUE, Dec 2 - Nacala - Port working normally on a first come-first served basis. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally on a first come-first served basis. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally. Pilotage now possible 24 hours per day for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugs fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain.

Maputo - Pilotage now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 120 metres loa with a maximum draft of 9 metres. Two tugs (one out of order). Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangement with the port captain. All berths are working normally and expected to remain so (first come-first served basis). Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres plus the rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, Dec 2 - Walvis Bay - Port working norlly.

SOUTH AFRICA, Dec 2 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Working normally. Bulk import berths - Working normally. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Working normally. Import berths belt system will be out of action for maintenance from 8-14/12. Bulk coal berths - 14 Vessels anchored awaiting berthing/loading turns with berthing delays of approx. 4 days being experienced. The congestion problem should ease up by the beginning of next week. Durban - Container terminal - Delays of up to 54 hours being experienced at present. Point/New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (maydon wharf 8) - One sunflower loader for December. Bunker supplies - Fluid. Delays of 4-6 hours in supplying bunkers can be expected due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - Fully booked for December and January 1997.

East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths - Extremely busy but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Fully booked for December and up to mid-January 1997, thereafter open for bookings. Copper - Moving in small parcels of 2,500 tonnes per month in containers to the Far East. Gas Oil pipeline - Under utilised. Wheat imports - Two vessels due mid-December. Log loaders - One vessel due end-December. Tankers - Expected to be busy until end December. Port Elizabeth - Port working normally with 3 vessels in port. No delays expected on general, tanker or ore berths. Container berth - Three vessels due 5/12 with no delays expected.

Cape Town - Breakbulk berths - No delays expected for coming week. Container terminal - No major delays expected for the coming week. Bunker berths - No delays for the coming week. Dry-docks, repair quay - Fully occupied at present, with booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, Nov 30 - Sfax - Six vessels in port of which 5 discharging (1 bulk yellow corn, 1 bulk wheat, 1 fuel oil, 1 general cargo, 1 containers), 1 loading steel. Sousse - Two vessels in port of which 1 discharging cotton, 1 awaiting orders, no waiting time. Tunis - One vessel discharging marble chips. Rades - Four ro/ros. La Goulette - North side - 1 Cereal vessel discharging maize, 1 passenger vessel, 1 general cargo vessel. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 motor tanker, 2 vessels in roads.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, Nov 24-30 - Dubai - 182 Vessels of which 79 containers, 17 general cargo, 5 general cargo/containers, 4 bulkers, 6 car carriers, 11 tankers, 2 naval, 1 livestock, 5 for bunkers/ repairs/stores, 3 dhows, 12 barges, 9 tugs, 24 supply, 2 lpg tankers, 1 VLCC, 1 rig. 4 Container vessels loading at berth, 9 discharging (6 general cargo, 3 tankers). 11 Under repair/laid-up (2 general, 9 tankers). 29 Containers, 8 general, 3 tankers due.

YEMEN, Dec 1 - Hodeidah - Berths 1, 2, 4 and 5 occupied, all other berths vacant. Three vessels berthed of which 1 sugar, 1 general cargo, 1 passenger. No vessels at anchorage. Berthing delays, general cargo up to 1 day, bagged cargoes up to 2 days, bulk cargo up to 4 days, containers up to 6 days. Mokha - One vessel berthed discharging wheatflour, no vessels anchored, no berthing delays. Hodeidah - Three vessels berthed of which 1 sugar, 1 panamax, 1 rice/general cargo. 1 vessel at anchor awaiting bunkers. No delays for containers/reefers/general cargo (steel, timber, powder) bagged cargo (sugar, rice, flour, bulk wheat/corn.
